name: Tessera Corponation Acoustic Null Field Emitter
product_name: Tessera Corponation Acoustic Null Field Emitter
description:
The Acoustic Null Field Emitter is a palm-sized device that projects a directional anti-phase sound field, effectively creating a cone of acoustic cancellation extending up to four meters from the emitter's face. Tessera Corponation's approach differs from conventional white-noise maskers by targeting the precise frequency signatures of the user's movement and speech in real time — an onboard microphone array samples incoming sound at sub-millisecond latency, generates inverted waveforms, and emits them through a phased array of micro-transducers, canceling the user's acoustic output before it propagates beyond the null cone's boundary.

The device's most technically notable characteristic is its adaptive notch filtering, which allows it to suppress the user's sounds while leaving environmental noise largely intact within the cone — meaning the user can still hear their surroundings clearly while remaining acoustically invisible to listeners outside the field. This bidirectional selectivity is computationally intensive and is the primary driver of the unit's relatively short active window on a single charge. At maximum range and fidelity, the emitter sustains approximately ninety minutes of continuous operation before requiring a recharge or cell swap.

Tessera developed the Emitter originally for use by their Lattice network installation crews, who frequently work in acoustically monitored corporate infrastructure. The device moved rapidly into the broader market when early production units were acquired by several high-profile extraction teams and demonstrated in field conditions. Tessera's official position is that the product is sold for 'sensitive facility maintenance applications,' a description that has satisfied regulators in three of GLMZ's six administrative sectors.

specifications.suppression_effectiveness: ~94% for speech, ~87% for movement noise (hard surfaces)
specifications.operating_modes: Active null (full suppression), Whisper mode (speech only, extended battery), Passive monitor (no emission, audio logging only)

tactical_use: Clipped to a harness or held in the lead hand during movement through acoustically monitored spaces. Most effective for small teams of one to three operators moving in close formation within the null cone's arc. Larger teams require multiple units with overlapping coverage. Whisper mode is commonly used during static observation phases to extend battery life. The device does not suppress sound produced outside the user's immediate body — closing a door or dropping equipment will still register on external sensors.
cultural_context: The Acoustic Null Field Emitter has a reputation in GLMZ's infiltration community as a 'professional's tool' — compact, effective, and expensive enough to filter out amateurs. Its association with Tessera Corponation's infrastructure crews has given it a degree of plausible deniability that operatives prize. In corporate security briefings, the device is increasingly listed as a primary threat multiplier for intrusion scenarios, and several firms have begun deploying redundant vibration-sensor networks specifically to counter its effectiveness on hard flooring.
known_users: Investigative journalists operating in surveilled zones
Corporate counter-intelligence teams (reversed — used to detect users)
The Stillwater Group (a known freelance operations collective in GLMZ)
story_hooks: An Acoustic Null Field Emitter is found at the scene of a high-security assassination — the device was left behind deliberately, suggesting either a setup or a panicked exit. Its serial number traces to a Tessera corporate procurement order that officially doesn't exist.

A player's contact needs to pass a message in a room known to be acoustically monitored. They need a Null Emitter, but every unit in the district has been bought up in the last 48 hours by someone preparing for a major operation.

Tessera quietly pushes a firmware update that adds a telemetry ping to all registered Emitters — a whistleblower inside the company warns operatives that their operational movements may now be logged.

A new vibration-sensor countermeasure has been installed in a target facility specifically designed to detect the micro-transducer harmonic signature of the Tessera Emitter, turning the device into a liability rather than an asset.
